title: hzxie/DynamicVLA
summary: DynamicVLA is the official code release for a vision-language-action model aimed at manipulating dynamic objects, where the robot has to reason over changing visual scenes rather than static pick-and-place setups. The available description is thin, but the project appears to package the implementation behind the arXiv paper “DynamicVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation,” making it useful for researchers who want to inspect or reproduce the model rather than just read the paper.

title: google-deepmind/mujoco_playground
summary: MuJoCo Playground is an open-source library for training robot policies with GPU-accelerated simulation and moving them toward real-world deployment. It is aimed at robot learning workflows where fast iteration, scalable reinforcement learning, and sim-to-real transfer matter, using MuJoCo as the physics backbone.

extra.full_text: An open-source library for GPU-accelerated robot learning and sim-to-real transfer.

title: NVIDIA/warp
summary: NVIDIA Warp is a Python toolkit for writing GPU-accelerated simulation and computation kernels, aimed at workloads in robotics, physics simulation, and machine learning. It is useful when researchers need fast differentiable or high-throughput simulation code while staying in a Python-centered workflow.

extra.full_text: A Python framework for GPU-accelerated simulation, robotics, and machine learning.

title: RobotControlStack/robot-control-stack
summary: RobotControlStack is a lean sim-to-real stack for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action models and reinforcement-learning agents without ROS. It provides native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for common robot platforms including Franka, UR5e, xArm, and SO101, making it useful for researchers who want a lighter path from simulation experiments to real robot control.

extra.full_text: A lean, ROS-free sim-to-real framework for training and deploying Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and RL agents. Native MuJoCo Gymnasium wrappers with synchronous execution for Franka, UR5e, xArm, and SO101.

title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab-Arena
summary: Isaac Lab - Arena extends NVIDIA Isaac Lab with a composable robotics simulation layer for building and evaluating robot-learning environments at scale. It is aimed at quickly mixing robot embodiments, objects, task setups, and scene configurations, making it useful for prototyping policies and comparing how they behave across diverse simulated conditions.

extra.full_text: Isaac Lab - Arena is a robotics simulation framework that enhances NVIDIA Isaac Lab by providing a composable, scalable system for creating diverse simulation environments and evaluating robot learning policies. The framework enables developers to rapidly prototype and test robotic tasks with various robot embodiments, objects, and environments.

title: iit-DLSLab/basic-locomotion-isaaclab
summary: An IsaacLab DirectEnv implementation for training and testing basic quadruped locomotion, with support for multiple robot platforms rather than a single fixed morphology. It is aimed at practical policy development workflows, including sim-to-sim transfer and sim-to-real deployment, so it is useful as a starting point for researchers who want a compact locomotion environment that connects simulation training to real robot experiments.

title: dartsim/dart
summary: DART is a research-focused C++23 physics engine for robotics, animation, and machine learning, with Python bindings for easier integration into experiments and tooling. It is useful when a project needs simulation infrastructure that can sit close to robotics or ML workflows while still exposing a modern C++ core.

title: RoboVerseOrg/RoboVerse
summary: RoboVerse aims to unify robot learning infrastructure by packaging a platform, dataset, and benchmark around scalable, generalizable robot behavior. It is meant to give researchers a common place to build and evaluate robot learning methods across tasks, reducing the usual fragmentation between simulation, data collection, and benchmarking.

extra.full_text: RoboVerse: Towards a Unified Platform, Dataset and Benchmark for Scalable and Generalizable Robot Learning

title: iLearn-Lab/CVPR26-OptimusVLA
summary: OptimusVLA is the official implementation of a CVPR 2026 vision-language-action model for robotic manipulation that combines a global prior with local consistency through a dual-memory design. The interesting part is the memory mechanism: it augments action generation with broader task-level context while preserving locally coherent manipulation behavior, aiming to make robot control more efficient and reliable.

title: learnsyslab/clare
summary: CLARE is the official codebase for a RA-L 2026 method that keeps vision-language-action models learning over time by routing inputs through adapters and autonomously expanding those adapters when needed. The interesting part is the continual-learning mechanism: instead of retraining or relying on a fixed adapter set, it manages task-specific capacity through adapter routing and growth, aiming to preserve prior robot skills while adapting to new ones.

extra.full_text: [RA-L 2026] Official code repository for "CLARE: Continual Learning for Vision-Language-Action Models via Autonomous Adapter Routing and Expansion".
